extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), and members of the public considering filing protests under 37 CFR 1.291
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for filing, serving, and Office/examiner treatment of written protests against pending patent applications under 37 CFR 1.291, including timing, content, evidence, and limitations on protestor participation. Guidance covers original and reissue applications, examiner actions, and restrictions on multiple/cumulative protests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who Can Protest
rubrics_metrics.description: Any member of the public, including private persons, corporate entities, and government agencies, may file a protest under 37 CFR 1.291. A protest may be filed by an attorney or other representative on behalf of an unnamed real party in interest. 37 CFR 1.291 does not require that the real party in interest be identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a protest is not the first protest by the real party in interest, compliance with 37 CFR 1.291(c)(5) is required. The requirements cannot be avoided by multiple protests submitted by different people representing the same real party in interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of Protest (When Should the Protest Be Submitted)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except where accompanied by the written consent of the applicant, a protest must be submitted prior to the date the application was published under 37 CFR 1.211 or the mailing of a notice of allowance under 37 CFR 1.311, whichever occurs first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protests should be filed as soon as possible after learning of the application to maximize consideration. A protest submitted after mailing of a notice of allowance may still be considered if it clearly anticipates or renders claims obvious, but likelihood of consideration decreases as allowance approaches. Special rules apply for reissue applications (see reissue-related criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of the Application (Adequate Identification / Matching)
rubrics_metrics.description: A protest must specifically identify the application to which the protest is directed by application number or serial number and filing date (and other identifying data if possible) so it can be matched with the application file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended identifying information to include: Name of applicant(s); Application number (mandatory); Filing date; Title of invention; Group art unit number (if known); Name of examiner (if known); Current status and location of application (if known); and the word 'ATTENTION:' followed by the area of the Office. Inadequate identification may prevent matching and result in return or discard of the protest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content Requirements of a Protest (37 CFR 1.291(c) substantive list)
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to identification and service requirements, a protest must include: (1) a listing of the patents, publications, or other information relied upon; (2) a concise explanation of the relevance of each item listed; (3) a copy of each listed patent, publication, or other item, or at least the pertinent portions; (4) an English language translation of all necessary and pertinent parts of any non-English item relied upon; and (5) for second/subsequent protests by same party in interest, explanations per 1.291(c)(5) plus a processing fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protestors are encouraged to use form PTO/SB/08A and 08B (or equivalent) for listing prior art. Initial protest submission must be complete because protestor will not be given an opportunity to supplement incomplete protests (active participation ends with filing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Service Requirement (37 CFR 1.291(b) & 1.248)
rubrics_metrics.description: The protest will be entered into the record only if the protest has been served upon the applicant in accordance with § 1.248, or filed with the Office in duplicate if service is not possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manner of service may be: personal delivery; leaving at usual place of business with employee; leaving at residence with suitable person; transmission by first-class mail (date of mailing is date of service); or, if practicable methods are not available, publication in the Official Gazette. Papers required to be served must contain proof of service (date and manner, and in case of personal service, name of person served).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to File Duplicate if Service Not Possible
rubrics_metrics.description: If service upon the applicant is not possible, the protest should be filed with the Office in duplicate so the Office can attempt service on the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a duplicate is enclosed for the applicant, include an explanation of why service on applicant could not be made. If no duplicate is filed and no indication of service, the Office may contact applicant to determine service status or request a duplicate before referring to examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial Office Handling and Entry into File
rubrics_metrics.description: A protest specifically identifying the application and complying with 37 CFR 1.291(a), (b), and (c) will be entered in the application file and referred to the assigned examiner if matched in time to permit review during prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not timely matched due to inadequate identification, the protest may be returned or discarded. Protests filed with applicant's written consent will be entered even if after publication but must still be matched in time to permit examiner review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement of Receipt (Self-Addressed Postcard)
rubrics_metrics.description: A member of the public filing a protest will not receive communications from the Office relating to the protest other than return of a self-addressed postcard included with the protest to acknowledge receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return of the postcard is not an indication the protest complies with 37 CFR 1.291. The postcard will not indicate whether an application exists or its status (confidentiality rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protestor Participation Limits (37 CFR 1.291(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Active participation by a protestor ends with filing of the protest. Protestor will not receive communications, may not participate in interviews, cannot appeal to the Board, and the Office will not serve prosecution documents on protestors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No further submissions on behalf of the protestor will be considered unless submitted under 37 CFR 1.291(c)(5) (second/subsequent protests complying with requirements). Protestor may not complete incomplete protests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on Multiple/Cumulative Protests by Same Real Party in Interest (37 CFR 1.291(c)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple piecemeal or cumulative protests by the same real party in interest are not permitted. Additional cumulative prior art by the same real party in interest will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A second or subsequent protest by the same real party in interest must include (A) an explanation why the issues raised are significantly different than earlier ones, (B) why the significantly different issues were not presented earlier, and (C) payment of the processing fee under 37 CFR 1.17(i). Failure to comply will result in non-entry, return, or discard of the protest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of Information That Can Be Relied On in a Protest
rubrics_metrics.description: Any information which, in the protestor’s opinion, would make the grant of a patent improper can be relied upon, not limited to prior art documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include information demonstrating public knowledge or use (35 U.S.C. 102(a)/(b)), public use or sale (102(b)), abandonment (102(c)), that applicant did not invent (102(f)), inventorship issues (102(g)), insufficiency of disclosure or failure to disclose best mode (35 U.S.C. 112), fraud or violation of duty of disclosure (37 CFR 1.56), and any other information demonstrating non-compliance with statutory patentability requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible Evidence Forms and Considerations (authentication & probative value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conventional prior art (patents and printed publications) are most common, but other evidence (litigation materials, complaints, depositions, exhibits, affidavits/declarations, orders, invoices, delivery schedules, etc.) may be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evidence other than prior art documents is relied upon, authentication and probative value issues may arise and must be evaluated; trade secret or court-protected information may be submitted but will be treated per MPEP § 724 and may be made public if a reasonable examiner considers it important to deciding whether to allow the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner Must Conduct Normal Examination and Search
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing of a protest does not relieve the examiner from conducting a normal examination on the merits, including the required search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence submitted in a protest will be considered on the same basis as other ex parte evidence (In re Reuter). Examiner must consider documents and issues raised by the protest when the protest is timely entered in the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner Initial Review Checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of a protest, the examiner will immediately review: (A) whether service on applicant is indicated or a duplicate filed; and (B) whether the protest raises fraud/inequitable conduct or duty of disclosure issues (which will be entered generally without comment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If service is not indicated and no duplicate filed, examiner should determine if service was made by contacting applicant or applicant's attorney/agent (not the protestor). If service not made, bring protest and file to TC Director for action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant Opportunity to Comment / Examiner Requests for Information (37 CFR 1.291(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: If necessary, the examiner may offer applicant an opportunity to file comments (usually one month) or may require applicant to reply to the protest and answer specific questions under 37 CFR 1.291(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions to applicant must be limited to those reasonably necessary for the examiner to decide the issues raised by the protest. Examiner may not require reply to questions relating to fraud/inequitable conduct/duty of disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's Obligation to Consider and Document Protested Prior Art and Arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: If a protest is timely entered and complies with 1.291(c), the examiner must consider each of the prior art or other documents submitted and any non-prior art issues raised, and must make evident by detailed reasoning the examiner’s position as to the major arguments and points raised by the protestor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While not required to answer every minor point, the major arguments must be specifically covered. Arguments related to fraud/inequitable conduct/duty of disclosure are not to be treated or discussed by the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking Considered References and Reporting Consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: For prior art or other documents the examiner relies on in rejecting claims, the examiner will place such documents of record by means of form PTO-892, or if the protestor used PTO/SB/08A and 08B the examiner places initials adjacent to the citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examiner considers documents not submitted in full, examiner should mark 'checked' and initial adjacent to the reference or 'All checked' in the margin; indicate in the next Office action that all documents submitted have been considered. If documents listed but not considered, draw a line through the citation on PTO/SB/08A/08B.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of Protests Filed After Publication or Allowance (without applicant consent)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a protest is submitted after publication or mailing of notice of allowance and is not accompanied by the applicant's written consent, it should not be entered in the application file and the applicant should be notified that the protest is untimely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the protest includes an indication of service on applicant, the original protest should be discarded. If service is not indicated, the duplicate (if present) should be discarded and the original sent to applicant with notification of nonentry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of Protests Filed After Publication or Allowance (with applicant consent)
rubrics_metrics.description: A protest may be filed at any time if accompanied by the written consent of the applicant; the protest will be entered into the record (subject to matching with the intended application and compliance with other requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The written consent should indicate consent to the specific protest being submitted (applicant may give blanket consent or specific consent). The Office will enter the protest only if it is within the scope of the consent and complies with 37 CFR 1.291(b) (other than timeliness) and (c). Even with consent, timely matching for examiner review may not be possible if submitted close to publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incomplete Protests and Protestor's Inability to Supplement
rubrics_metrics.description: A protest must be complete on initial submission; a protestor may not complete an incomplete protest, nor further participate in, or inquire about, Office proceedings relating to the initial protest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improper or incomplete protests will be returned or discarded at the option of the Office. The Office will not consider later submissions from the protestor unless compliant with 37 CFR 1.291(c)(5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue Application Special Timing Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A protest filed in a reissue application is not a preissuance opposition (since the original patent has been granted) and may be filed throughout the pendency of the reissue application prior to mailing of a notice of allowance, but typically should be filed within the 2-month period following announcement of the reissue application in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a protest cannot be filed within the 2-month period, the protest can be submitted later but may be received after examiner action; extensions may be requested by petition under 37 CFR 1.182 with fee and justification, filed prior to expiration of the 2-month period. If prosecution on the merits has been closed, a petition under 1.182 and fee may be required with the protest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fraud/Inequitable Conduct Issues Entered but Not Commented On (37 CFR 1.291(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a protest raising inequitable conduct issues satisfies entry provisions, it will be entered into the application file generally without comment on the inequitable conduct issues raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners will not treat or discuss those arguments or points directed to 'fraud,' 'inequitable conduct,' or 'violation of duty of disclosure' in Office actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade Secret / Court-Protected Information Submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Information subject to court-imposed protective or secrecy orders, or trade secret information obtained by agreement, may be submitted with a protest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such information will be treated in accordance with MPEP § 724 and may be made public if a reasonable examiner would consider it important in deciding whether to allow the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting Results and Referral for Litigation-Related Matters
rubrics_metrics.description: After considering the protest, the examiner will report the results of consideration to the Technology Center (TC) Director. If a reissue application is related to a patent involved in litigation or a pending interference, the application should be referred to the Office of Patent Legal Administration before considering the protest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protests relating to litigation should be marked 'REISSUE LITIGATION' on the envelope and top right-hand portion of the protest and mailed to Mail Stop Petition per guidance; petitions to delay reissue examination may be requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of Prior Art to Issued Patents (37 CFR 1.501(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate from protests, any person at any time during the enforceability period of a patent may cite to the Office, in writing, prior art consisting of patents and printed publications believed to be pertinent to the patent (37 CFR 1.501(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 2202–2208 for guidance on citation of prior art to patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office Communication Constraints to Protect Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Office personnel must exercise care to ensure substantive matters relating to an application are not discussed ex parte with a protestor or communicated in writing ex parte to a protestor; examiners must not communicate in any manner with the protestor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original applications are confidential unless published or otherwise available under the regulations; postcard acknowledgements will not reveal application existence or status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of Documents Not Submitted in Full Conformance
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should not be overly technical in construing 37 CFR 1.291(c) and should consider a protest to the extent it is helpful even if one or more of the listed items is omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examiner considers documents not submitted in full, the examiner must mark them as considered ('checked' with initials or equivalent) and indicate in the next Office action that the documents were considered; protestor cannot be assured examiner will consider missing documents.
